main_text.p: mam Ægæum pelagus spectantem Locri Opontii & Epicnemides in orâ sunt interpositi, easque modico intervallo separant. Sed ad Ætoliam revertor, ob quam ista heic sunt præmissa aut repetita. Habet à septentrione accolas partem Amphilochorum, Athamanes populum ferum & barbarum, Perrhœbos, Ænianos Oetæos. Reliquos terminos jam diximus. Habitata fuit variis populis, parte Athamanum, Tymphæis, Ephyris, Ænienfibus, Perrhœbis, Dolopibus, Maracibus, Atracibus, ut eos recenset Plinius. Strabo verò libro x hos memorat: Ophienses, Eurytanes, quos maximum Ætoliæ populum fuisse, & ὠμοφάγυς[?], cruda carne scilicet vescentes, & linguâ ignotissimos, Thucydides perhibet: item Agræos, Curetos, aliosque. Idem Strabo distinguit eam in veterem & novam vel acquisitam medio Eveno fluvio à septentrione è montibus vicinis in mare Ionium defluente. Et veterem dicit inter Acheloum & Evenum jacentem planam & magis fœcundam fuisse: alteram ab Eveno ad Locros Ozolas asperiorem, & minus fertilem. Vrbes Ætolorum præcipuæ fuêre Calydon ad Evenum fluvium, vii millibus passuum & quingentis à mari remota, Pleuron in mediter-

page.notes: Right and left margins carry only faint show-through and stains from the other side of the leaf, plus a few marks that are not printed text; none is transcribed. The Greek word ὠμοφάγυς is read from a small scan and is doubtful. The text ends in mid-word "mediter-" and continues on the next page. The top right shows a faint "201" that is marked as doubtful in the page number. The running head's first word is clear, but the faint print at the top may hide a few letters.
